logp.method_description: Partition coefficients (Pow), defined as Pow = corg/caq, where corg and caq are the molar concentrations of the selected compound in the n-octanol and aqueous phase, respectively, were determined by the shake-flask method and UV–Vis measurements, according to a previously described procedure [37,75,76]. The stock solution of a selected compound (ca 3 mg) was prepared by first adding CH2Cl2 (ca 30 μL to help solubilization), followed by water-saturated octanol (2.5 mL). The stock solution was diluted with water-saturated octanol (1.2 mL stock + 2.8 mL water-saturated octanol; TOT ca. 4 mL) so that the absorbance in the region of interest is between 1.5 and 2 at λmax. After recording the UV–vis spectrum, an aliquot of the diluted solution (Vorg = 1.2 mL) was transferred into a centrifuge tube and exactly 1.2 mL of octanol-saturated water was added. The mixture was vigorously stirred for 20 min then centrifuged (7 min × 3900 rpm). The UV–vis spectrum of the organic phase was recorded (Aforg) and the partition coefficient was calculated as Pow = Aforg - Aback/(A0org - Aforg) where A0org and Aforg are the absorbance in the organic phase before and after partition with the aqueous phase respectively and while Aback is the absorbance of the organic solvent. The wavelength corresponding to a well-defined maximum of shoulder absorption of each compound (320–400 nm range) was used for UV–Vis quantitation. The procedure was repeated three times for each sample (from the same stock solution); results are given as mean ± standard deviation (Table 2). All operations were carried out at room temperature (21 ± 1 °C).
